title: Make Your Idea Playable
intro: A hands-on Claude session for CASBS fellows. In about five messages you will turn one idea from your own research into a small interactive simulation or demo that anyone can play with, then save it as an app on your computer.

facts.label: What you need:
facts.text: a Claude Pro account and the Claude app or claude.ai open. About 20 minutes.

facts.label: Chat or Cowork?
facts.text: If your Claude app has both, use Chat.

facts.label: What you end up with:
facts.text: an interactive artifact built around your own idea. Good for a class, a talk, or a curious colleague.

facts.label: As of 11/25:
facts.text: installing the artifact as an app on your computer works on a regular Claude account, but not (yet) on the Claude for Education accounts.

steps.title: Step 1: Pitch it
steps.before: Start a new chat and paste this, filling in the brackets.
steps.prompt: I study [field]. One idea from my work is: [2-3 sentences, for example "small individual preferences can produce large-scale segregation"]. Suggest three different ways to turn this into a small interactive artifact someone could play with in two minutes. Don't build yet.
steps.after: Read the three options and pick the one you would most want to show someone.

steps.title: Step 2: Build it
steps.prompt: Build option [number] as an artifact. Give it sliders or controls for the key assumptions, and a one-paragraph "what you're looking at" panel.
steps.after: Play with it. Move every control. Notice what feels wrong.
steps.note: Claude asks before it publishes the artifact, and the box notes that artifacts aren't HIPAA eligible. Note that artifacts are hosted on Anthropic servers.

noteImage.alt: Claude's Publish artifact box: uploads the file to claude.ai as a new artifact, which stays private until you share it, with a note that artifacts are not HIPAA eligible; buttons Publish and Deny

steps.title: Step 3: Argue with it
steps.prompt: Now act as a skeptical reviewer in my field. What does this model oversimplify or get wrong? Then add one control that lets the viewer switch on the most important complication.
steps.after: Read the critique like a peer review. Where is it right? Where is it shallow? Tell Claude.

steps.title: Step 4: Make it yours
steps.prompt: Add a "try this" section with three experiments for the viewer, give it a memorable name, and make the design feel like [a 1970s journal / a board game / a field notebook].

steps.title: Step 5: Keep it
steps.before: Ask for any last changes in plain words, for example "make the text larger" or "the default settings should show the surprising case first".
how: When you are happy, click the artifact's name at the top of it to open its menu.
Choose Install as app to keep it as a desktop app on your Mac or Windows computer, or Share to copy its link.

items.text: Run 100 underpowered studies and see what gets "published".

tips.title: Tips
items: Talk to Claude the way you would brief a sharp research assistant. Say what you want and why.
If the result is wrong, say exactly what is wrong. "The curve should flatten after the threshold" works better than "fix it".
You are the expert on the idea. Claude builds fast, and you decide whether the model is honest.
